6dfdb95c3e575ae33e64.text: In this part of the module, you will learn the concept of bias and ways to

1c630973f97d1a0251fa.text: Bias refers to an author’s expression of his/her own opinion on a particular

a21171d19a36b12fce76.text: issue without examining and presenting enough evidences. This arises from the author’s thinking which may be influenced by personal beliefs, culture, attitudes, preferences, and past experiences.

7e708af52c02af127d87.text: To further understand bias in writing, refer to the illustration below

ca784a03bc4ba2100ada.text: When does an author become bias?

5697f28122bd10103354.text: An author becomes bias when he/she persuades the reader to believe on

c2ff01bee6b93a17186f.text: his/her own stand of the issue by giving inaccurate information or false impression even with or without the intention of misleading the readers.

980e898d9ada197df8c0.text: How do you determine the author’s biases?

30b6f804231c226b2ca0.text: To determine the author’s biases and to understand his/her underlying

5a01e6504c86a07264d8.text: purpose, you must look at the use of evidence and diction.

3184e77bb57ffdd344f0.text: Evidences can be in a form of facts and information, testimonies and direct

9401879f55e7d5de4b3b.text: observations, scientific and legal findings, and anecdotes and philosophical evidences.

9adac36daab5db6d9607.text: Diction refers to the words or expressions that help convey the stand of the

74f751115a6779550aff.text: author towards an issue. These words and expressions may indicate a positive or negative connotation or meaning.

62235c79e4f5dd181b5f.text: The table below shows an example of a word with a positive and a negative

666a69df12195f9f9181.text: My new neighbor is a mature woman.

8f8881fed598cf715940.text: My new neighbor looks too mature in that dress.

4bd24e9878dba1502a53.text: woman looks old in her dress.

0cbb1858b3d6d2f1e34b.text: Here are some guide questions to check the author’s use of evidence.  Does the author present more positive evidences to support one side of an issue?  Does the author present more negative evidences to disprove one side of an issue?

4910753a83fedf129004.text: Here are some guide questions to check the author’s diction.  Does the author use more positive words and expressions to present one side of an issue?  Does the author use more negative words and expressions to present one side of an issue?

c614962378357b199f96.text: Let’s use the guide questions above when we read and examine the paragraph below:

c9b05630b6aa9ff48f8a.text: Summer vacation is the favorite season for most people. Some go to the

abc1a843b2abfa5166c7.text: beach; others go to the mountains. These places will make them feel closer to nature. However, having a vacation by the sea differs from having a vacation in the mountains.

1887216dbf556ddd88bc.text: People can swim, surf, or dive on the beach. Others can pick up shells, go

6ad6befcd5be4a3b32a1.text: sunbathing, or even play volleyball. Also, the sound of the sea waves hitting the shore can make people feel more relaxed. While sitting on wooden chairs, people can watch the sun as it sets down.

6d8808628ae8e38f7447.text: On the other hand, people can also explore the mountain side to experience

34a52c5f06220f83319e.text: the strong and fresh air. People can hike and do bonfire. However, hiking in the mountains can be dangerous because of the presence of wild animals and the danger of falling.

30da98e7a47941902302.text: Whichever, people choose, they can experience a lot of enjoyable adventure.

cba1157cddd7b3c7e45a.text: Yet, there are many things people can do in the beach than in the mountain.

cddf796dfbb69dd0cad7.text: Following the guide questions given in the discussion, let’s analyze the

417be45f20bfdfe751ed.text: evidences and the diction used by the author.

82281fcecca7b386880a.text:  has a strong and fresh air

2b5a96d5cb6d98757b31.text:  can pick up shells, go sunbathing,

d20f06f0b9dcab0eba10.text:  can make people feel more relaxed

64a682a5f1d1fae1d4fb.text:  presence of wild animals and the

f2e67387d94e6d70a67e.text:  can watch the sun as it sets down

4ccf0843329991316ba7.text: Based on the table above, you will notice that the author has presented more

e4b12406b97621fb8361.text: positive evidences of going to the beach than going to the mountain.

aff026f385ad025de808.text: You will also notice that there is an unfair presentation of the evidences. The

ab5537a844775da03b21.text: author emphasized the dangers on going to the mountain but failed to present the dangers on going to the beach like drowning.

5f068687ce2cd8a6fb39.text: The author used more positive words such as highlighting the benefits of going

58ad2c26d01be086412e.text: to the beach, but he/she used negative words when referring to going to the mountain such as dangerous and danger. These words give a negative impression to the readers making the author biased as he/she was favoring one idea over the other. He/she also failed to present both advantages and disadvantages about going to the beach and going to the mountain in a more balanced and objective way.
